newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks close lower in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks close lower in thin trade.

text.p: Sri Lankan stocks closed slightly lower in thin trade on Friday as investors waited to see which way the market would go after recent sharp gains, brokers said.
The Colombo Stock Exchange all share index closed 2.7 points lower at 823.4 on a low turnover of 33.2 million rupees, against 94 million on Thursday.
"Investors are going to sit out the weekend and come back on Monday and volumes are likely to pick up," said Sarinda Unamboowe of brokerage John Keells.
He said big investors keen on blue chip stocks were holding back mostly due to low liquidity in the market.
"We have some buy orders and hope to conclude deals next week," he said.
A broker with CT Smith said foreign buying, which has increased sharply in recent weeks, was lower on Friday and hit market sentiment.
"The market should go up next week but if it climbs too fast a correction could set in," the broker said.
Ceylon Cold Stores rose 4.75 rupees to 194.75 rupees and Commercial Bank was up five rupee to 230. John Keells Holdings rose three rupees to 345.
